Answer: C
Reason: The chest X-ray demonstrates multiple bilateral pulmonary nodules, some of which appear to have cavitation or central lucency (particularly in the right lower zone). This radiographic pattern of multiple nodules with necrosis/cavitation, combined with the clinical presentation of chest pain and non-productive cough, is characteristic of Necrotizing Sarcoid Granulomatosis (NSG), a rare variant of sarcoidosis. While Wegener's granulomatosis also presents with cavitary nodules, NSG is specifically defined by this histologic and radiographic overlap of sarcoid-like granulomas and necrotizing vasculitis.
